column1: # tests/os-release/expected.tsv -- what each fixture in this directory must
# resolve to, against BOTH matrix files the test reads. Tab-separated, SEVEN
# columns, one row per fixture:
#   fixture  id  version_id  tier_shipped  row_shipped  tier_pinned  row_pinned
#   fixture       the file name in this directory
#   id            the ID field the parser must read out of it
#   version_id    the VERSION_ID field the parser must read out of it, which
#                 may legitimately be EMPTY -- see debian-testing below
#   tier_shipped  supported | legacy | unknown, against ../../support-matrix.yml
#   row_shipped   the row it matches there, or "-" when none
#   tier_pinned   the same, against support-matrix.pinned-example.yml
#   row_pinned    the row it matches there, or "-" when none
# WHY TWO PAIRS OF COLUMNS. The shipped support-matrix.yml has an EMPTY
# supported tier, honestly, because no upstream ref is pinned. Nothing could
# then ever resolve as supported, and the supported half of the reader -- the
# tier lookup, the supported-wins precedence, the summary -- would never be
# executed by any test in the tree. support-matrix.pinned-example.yml is a
# matrix as it will look once tools/pin-upstream.sh has run, so the last two
# columns exercise that half. Neither file is evidence that anything was ever
# installed anywhere; tests/MATRIX-STATUS.md is where that would live.
# THE ROW THAT EARNS THE SECOND PAIR: debian-13 is legacy against the shipped
# file and SUPPORTED against the pinned one, from the same fixture and the same
# code. debian:13 is listed in both tiers of the pinned example, which is the
# real case -- it is both what today's upstream accepts and one of the nine the
# old installer ran on -- and this row is what proves supported wins.
# WHY THIS FILE RESTATES THE ANSWER. It is a deliberate second statement, and
# the only one in the tree. A test that derived the answer with the same rule
# the code uses would agree with itself no matter what the rule was; the Mint
# truncation in particular is a rule that has to be asserted from outside, or a
# regression turning 21.3 into linuxmint:21.3 passes every test we have.
# support-matrix.yml stays the ONE place the tiers are declared: a row here is
# about one fixture, not about what we support.
# The six fixtures that match nothing in the shipped file each carry a distinct
# reason:
#   ubuntu-26.04   what upstream's gate accepts TODAY, and not one of the
#                  legacy nine. Unknown against the shipped file precisely
#                  because nothing is pinned; supported against the pinned one.
#                  It is also the only fixture with a comment line in it, which
#                  is what proves the os-release parser skips one.
#   almalinux      upstream accepts AlmaLinux 10 and this installer still
#                  cannot drive it -- no apt-get. It is the fixture that shows
#                  the supported tier is an INTERSECTION and not a copy of
#                  upstream's list. Note VERSION_ID="10.0", so the
#                  first-component rule is what a future almalinux:10 row would
#                  rely on.
#   debian-testing Debian testing publishes NO VERSION_ID at all. matrix_identify
#                  returns an empty version, and an empty version must match
#                  nothing rather than fall back to the id. This row is the one
#                  with two adjacent tabs, which is also what stops the
#                  manifest splitter from collapsing empty fields.
#   kali           an ID we have never heard of, and a date-shaped rolling
#                  version
#   raspbian       an ID we do not support, wearing ID_LIKE=debian and
#                  VERSION_ID=12. It matches debian:12 the moment anybody
#                  consults ID_LIKE. This is the fixture that stops that.
#                  Upstream accepts Raspbian at major 13; we still do not.
#   fedora         not a Debian derivative at all, no ID_LIKE, and an UNQUOTED
#                  VERSION_ID -- which is also the fixture that proves the
#                  parser does not require quotes.
# Order follows support-matrix.yml's legacy tier, then the supported-only
# release, then the negatives.
